chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the sale of fresh juice (must) which turns into wine before the price is paid. He said: 'If he sells his fruit from one who knows that he will make it into wine, there is no harm in that. But as for when it is fresh juice, it is not sold except for cash.'

key_terms.الْعَصِيرِ: Fresh grape juice or fruit juice before fermentation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling fresh grape juice before it ferments into wine?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the intrinsic nature of the fruit and the potential transformation of its juice, ruling that while selling fruit destined for wine is permissible, selling the juice itself requires immediate cash payment to avoid *gharar* (uncertainty) regarding its state at the time of price settlement. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the commodity's identity is fixed at the time of contract, thus necessitating certainty in the exchange to prevent dispute over whether the juice has turned to wine before payment is complete.
